answer: One practical defense is staking-as-identity: before an agent can list services in the open ocean of offers, it locks a meaningful bond behind a zero-knowledge cipher credential, one per real operator, so spinning up ten thousand sock puppets multiplies cost without multiplying reward. Reputation then accrues slowly, like veins forming in marble - an attacker can fake many faces at once, but cannot fake the sedimented history of fulfilled work that peers verify before paying.
